content.direction: A warm, cinematic, lived-in mid-2000s suburban Texas kid's bedroom shared by eight-year-old Shaz and his little brother, built as a real Pixar feature-film set with appealing chunky stylized forms, bold saturated color scripting in cobalt, tangerine, cherry red, sunflower yellow and teal, and warm motivated late-afternoon light. Golden Texas sunlight pours through slatted blinds on the left wall in strong striped shafts, pooling across a scuffed honey-toned wood floor, a big saturated patterned rug, and glowing dust. Along the rear wall stands a sturdy bunk bed with rumpled cobalt and tangerine kid bedding, pillows askew, with sneakers kicked below and toys tucked underneath. To one side sits a chunky mid-2000s CRT television with rounded casing, a generic game console and tangled controllers spilling onto the floor, its screen glowing soft color with no figures. Around the rug lie binders bursting with generic trading cards, rubber-banded card stacks, and a half-played card battle spread with swirling starburst backs carrying no writing. A small science corner holds a chunky toy microscope, magnifying glass, kid chemistry set with jewel-toned liquids, and a rock collection on a low dresser and shelf, plus a few spare kid sunglasses on the dresser top. The ceiling carries glow stars, the walls carry taped-up kid drawings showing only pictures of planets and beakers, a folded geometric-patterned prayer rug and prayer beads rest on a shelf, and a school backpack leans against the bunk. A sturdy wooden chair stands screen-right angled inward for the mother's future seat, facing an open standing patch screen-left for Shaz, with the wall areas directly behind their future faces kept visually open so faces will read while staying fully dressed and saturated. Framed at child eye level as a medium-wide view with room for a slow straight push toward a medium two-shot. Empty of people ONLY — never an empty set: strictly zero people, zero characters, zero silhouettes, including in reflections, window views, artwork and screen glow. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, logos, labels or signage anywhere — card faces, posters, TV glow, books, boxes and rug all use picture-only art; no trademarked characters or emblems appear. Characters will be composited later.
knownDetails: Shaz was 8 when he wanted to be a scientist, without knowing why.
Shaz remembers being quiet and wearing sunglasses everywhere as his signature style.
His mother became very excited when he said he wanted to be a scientist; he remembers she seemed proud of him.
He loved watching Yu-Gi-Oh GX together with his older sister 7 years older and little brother 2 years younger; the siblings collected and battled with trading cards.
Muslim family background from the locked memories.

Mid-2000s suburban Dallas/McKinney, Texas home era context; approved scene stages the mother seated lighting up with pride as quiet Shaz tells his dream. Room architecture and furnishings are interpreted staging, not documented remembered details.
proposedDetails: Proposed architecture: saturated teal-blue walls with scuffed honey wood floor, slatted blinds on left wall, glow stars on ceiling, taped-up kid drawings showing pictures only of planets and beakers.
Proposed bunk bed along rear wall with rumpled cobalt and tangerine kid bedding, pillows askew, sneakers below and toys tucked underneath to show a room shared with the little brother.
Proposed chunky mid-2000s CRT television with rounded casing, generic game console and tangled controllers spilling onto the floor; screen glows soft color with no figures.
Proposed trading-card play: binders bursting with generic cards, rubber-banded stacks, and half-played battle spread on the rug, all card backs and faces with abstract starburst art and no writing.
Proposed science corner: chunky toy microscope, magnifying glass, kid chemistry set with jewel-toned liquids, and rock collection arranged on low dresser and shelf.
Proposed dresser top: a few spare kid sunglasses alongside rocks and science toys.
Proposed shelf dressing: folded geometric-patterned prayer rug and prayer beads, school backpack leaning on bunk, sneakers, worn spots and scuffs for lived-in Texas kid life.
Proposed lighting: warm late-afternoon Texas sun through slatted blinds in strong striped shafts with soft room fill, keeping both future face positions readable without harsh glare.

Proposed picture-only rule: absolutely no text, letters, numbers, logos, labels or signage anywhere on cards, posters, TV glow, books, boxes or rug; generic designs only with no trademarked characters.
